_about: Every external account the distribution channels need, as code (owner, 2026-10-31: everything as code; 2026-11-02: a managed email the agents use for sign-ups). One row per account: where to sign up, which address to sign up with, which secrets and variables the workflows read, and which channels it switches on. Secret NAMES only; values live in the GitHub secret store. Creating the account stays with the owner (goals.md, Hard limits: registering accounts and publishing under the portfolio's public name). `node platform/distribution/setup.mjs` prints the checklist and checks this file against the workflows.

signup_address.purpose: the one address every portfolio platform account is registered with: sign-up confirmations, password resets and platform notices

accounts.name: GitHub (this repository)
steps: No new account: the workflows use their own GITHUB_TOKEN.
Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > Variables: set DISTRIBUTE_RELEASES=true (a weekly launches release) and DISTRIBUTE_TOOL_RELEASES=true (version tags for allow-listed tools).
Optional: DISTRIBUTE_GHCR=true (container images) and DISTRIBUTE_DESKTOP=true (desktop app builds).

accounts.name: Mail to accounts@marisstella.app (Cloudflare Email Routing)
steps: Do this before any sign-up below, or the confirmation emails bounce (the domain had no MX record on 2026-10-31).

Give the deploy token the Email Routing permissions listed at the top of platform/pages/cloudflare/email-routing.mjs, then run the cloudflare-email workflow with apply ticked. support@, hello@ and accounts@ then land in the agent-managed inbox (platform/edge/inbox.mjs); nothing is forwarded and there is no verification link.

Set the INBOX_TOKEN secret on the edge Worker (`npx wrangler secret put INBOX_TOKEN` in platform/edge, any long random string) and give agent sessions the same value as an environment variable, so they can read the inbox with `node platform/edge/read-inbox.mjs`.

accounts.name: Bluesky
steps: Sign up with accounts@marisstella.app. Say in the bio that the account is automated and posts new free tools and write-ups from the portfolio.
Settings > Privacy and security > App passwords: create one for this repository. Never store the account password.
Add secrets BSKY_HANDLE and BSKY_APP_PASSWORD, then set DISTRIBUTE_BLUESKY=true. Dry run first: node platform/distribution/bluesky.mjs

accounts.name: Mastodon (one instance that welcomes labelled bots)
steps: Pick an instance whose rules allow bot accounts and self-promotion of free software. Read its rules the day you sign up.
Sign up with accounts@marisstella.app and tick "This is a bot account" in the profile (the script refuses to post without it).
Preferences > Development > New application: scopes write:statuses and read:accounts only. Store the token as MASTODON_TOKEN.
Set MASTODON_INSTANCE (https URL), MASTODON_ACCT (the handle, for the hub's metrics) and DISTRIBUTE_MASTODON=true.

accounts.name: dev.to
steps: Sign up with accounts@marisstella.app (email sign-up, not a social login, so the account does not hang off a personal profile).
Settings > Extensions > DEV Community API Keys: generate one, store it as DEVTO_API_KEY, set DISTRIBUTE_DEVTO=true.
Articles are drafts until DEVTO_PUBLISH=true. Read the first few drafts before you set it.

accounts.name: Hashnode
steps: Sign up with accounts@marisstella.app and create one publication (blog).
Account settings > Developer: generate a personal access token, store it as HASHNODE_TOKEN.
Set HASHNODE_PUBLICATION_ID and DISTRIBUTE_HASHNODE=true. Posts are drafts until HASHNODE_PUBLISH=true.

accounts.name: npm registry
steps: Sign up with accounts@marisstella.app and turn on two-factor authentication (npm asks for it to publish).
Create an organisation for the scope (NPM_SCOPE); two names are taken by other projects without one (portfolio/distribution/README.md).
Access Tokens > Generate: a granular token limited to that scope, with an expiry. Store it as NPM_TOKEN; set NPM_SCOPE, DISTRIBUTE_NPM=true and, for the MCP server, DISTRIBUTE_MCP=true.

accounts.name: PyPI
steps: Sign up with accounts@marisstella.app and turn on two-factor authentication (PyPI requires it).
Account settings > API tokens: create one. Store it as PYPI_TOKEN and set DISTRIBUTE_PYPI=true.

accounts.name: Homebrew tap (a second GitHub repository)
steps: Create an empty public repository named homebrew-<something> under your account.
Create a fine-grained token with Contents: write on that repository only. Store it as HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN.
Set HOMEBREW_TAP_REPO (owner/name) and DISTRIBUTE_HOMEBREW=true. Needs the npm channel live first (formulae install the npm packages).

accounts.name: Meta: Threads, a Facebook Page, Instagram
steps: These hang off a personal Meta login: a Page is administered from a personal profile, and Threads and Instagram professional accounts link to it. So the sign-up address is yours, not accounts@. Contact email on the Page can still be hello@marisstella.app.
Create the Page and an Instagram professional account, then a Meta developer app with the permissions listed in node platform/distribution/hub.mjs platforms.
Store THREADS_TOKEN, FACEBOOK_PAGE_TOKEN, INSTAGRAM_TOKEN; set the IDs, INSTAGRAM_IMAGE_BASE and each DISTRIBUTE_* you want on. Each platform is independent.

accounts.name: Buttondown (opt-in email list)
steps: Decide the postal address every email must show (CAN-SPAM). That is the only decision here that is not a click.
Sign up with accounts@marisstella.app, set the reply-to to hello@marisstella.app, keep double opt-in on.
Store BUTTONDOWN_API_KEY and set DISTRIBUTE_EMAIL=true. Emails are drafts until EMAIL_SEND=true.
